stories.title: OBD capture -- serialize ObdConnection wrapper + fence orphaned timeout daemons (F-117/A-17, P0)
stories.completionNotes: US-441 CLOSED (bench). Wrapper-lock + epoch-fence capture fix (F-117/A-17). CHANGES: (1) obd_connection.py -- renamed _connectLock -> _ioLock = THE single lock guarding EVERY .obd access; new query(command, callerGeneration=None) holds _ioLock around self.obd.query() (the serialized read path); disconnect() now holds _ioLock around close(); connect() accepts callerGeneration + fences a superseded re-open; _generation counter (+1 per connect-success AND per disconnect) + activeGeneration(); new ObdConnectionSupersededError. (2) logger.py:220 (queryParameter) + :290 (_queryViaDecoder) now call self.connection.query(cmd) NOT .obd.query(cmd) -- the load-bearing GAP-1 sites that bypassed lifecycle. (3) lifecycle.py _runInitialConnectWithTimeout + _queryWithTimeout capture generation (new module fn _resolveGeneration, isinstance-int gate so MagicMock connections take the legacy no-gen path) and route the query daemon through connection.query(); daemons thread-named obd-connect-gen<N> / obd-query-<cmd>-gen<N> (heartbeat already obd-reconnect-heartbeat) = observability AC. (4) SimulatedObdConnection given activeGeneration()/query()/connect(callerGeneration=) API parity. TD-036 no-boot-hang PRESERVED (daemon+wall-clock shape untouched; only .obd access serialized). REAL-CONCURRENCY TEST (GAP-1 VC, non-mocked): tests/pi/obdii/test_obd_connection_thread_safety.py -- proves raw .obd.query() interleaves (RED discriminator) while wrapper query() serializes (maxConcurrent==1), epoch fence drops superseded query/connect, live reader never fenced, + ObdDataLogger read path vs orphan daemon on the SAME wrapper = no interleaving. AC6 Rule-10: specs/architecture.md new '### 3.5 OBD Connection Threading Model' (serialization + epoch fence) -- authorized by AC6 bound-here despite specs/ normally PM-owned; US-447 finalizes the top 'Last Updated' changelog entry + regression_manifest. stories.title: UpsMonitor slow-drain detection + flap-debounce (F-051)
stories.completionNotes: US-444 CLOSED (bench). Slow-drain detection + flap-debounce (F-051). CRITICAL SCOPE JUDGMENT: F-051's April-2026 ACs framed this as a BATTERY/EXTERNAL power-source flag, but SS-T4 (Atlas 2026-05-19) RETIRED power-source decisions from UpsMonitor -- getPowerSource() is now a loud NotImplementedError tripwire (the VCELL-trend source heuristic bricked the Pi 2026-05-18). US-444's current goal correctly reframes this as a battery-HEALTH signal ('gradual battery drain is caught without false alarms'), so I built a HEALTH verdict, NOT a source decision -- getPowerSource() tripwire untouched, no source-transition path reintroduced. CHANGES: (1) NEW src/pi/hardware/slow_drain_detector.py -- SlowDrainDetector, a pure hardware-free state machine over (timestamp, VCELL) samples emitting DrainState UNKNOWN/STABLE/SLOW_DRAIN. Rolling window (default 300s) + net-decline threshold (0.005V) trip the RAW verdict; a debounce (30s) commits a verdict only after the raw signal holds its new value continuously for the debounce interval (flap suppression); a partial ramp-up window returns UNKNOWN (honest-instrument, never a confident STABLE). All 3 thresholds are module DEFAULT_* constants + injectable ctor params (matches the existing DEFAULT_VCELL_* pattern; no magic numbers), GROUNDED in F-051 drain-tests 1-4 (Drain 4 ~0.034V/min; real idle drain >=~0.001V/min = 0.005V/5min, above noise floor) + the 2026-04-29 inverted-drill flap trace (4 transitions in 45s / 5s flaps -> 30s debounce suppresses all without missing a real >=2min-spaced transition). (2) ups_monitor.py -- extracted _pollOnce() so each poll tick feeds VCELL to BOTH the history buffer AND the detector on ONE shared timestamp; new getSlowDrainState() accessor (pure delegate); ctor gains slowDrainDetector injection + slowDrain{Window,DeclineThreshold,Debounce} params; default detector built if not injected (so HardwareManager gets it free, no config-wiring change). getTelemetry() shape UNCHANGED (no new key) to keep the telemetry-shape gate + downstream TelemetryLogger/DB stable -- slow-drain is exposed via its own accessor, scope stays inside UpsMonitor. GATES (in-loop, synchronous): 10 new detector unit tests + 3 new UpsMonitor wiring tests GREEN; full tests/pi/hardware/ GREEN (no regression from the _pollingLoop->_pollOnce refactor). ruff check PASS on all 4 files. NOTE FOR PM: mypy (strict) NOT run -- not installed in this dev env (.venv/system python both 'No module named mypy', same as US-441/442); code is fully strict-typed (DrainState enum, float/DrainState returns, float|None candidateSince, deque[tuple[float,float]]) -- run the mypy gate at integration. BENCH-verified per the sprint's BENCH-ONLY method; the 'UPS-drain rig' live confirm is a CIO/deploy bench action (feed a real declining VCELL trace and watch getSlowDrainState() flag SLOW_DRAIN within ~5-6min).

stories.title: Automated battery test on boot (F-054)
stories.completionNotes: US-445 CLOSED (bench). Boot-time battery test (F-054, scoped slice of the 4-story feature -- register-read + health-assessment + log-a-result; cadence/discharge/trend stories stay in F-054 backlog). KEY DESIGN CALL (the 'battery_health_log / state' fork): did NOT write battery_health_log -- that table is drain-EVENT-shaped (start/end/runtime, load_class production/test/sim, drain_event_id) and feeds drain-baseline analytics; a boot SNAPSHOT is not a drain event, and writing one there would pollute the baseline AND (per the US-442 note in battery_health.py) re-open the orphan-row risk class. Chose the 'state' target = the established F-103/F-097 honest-instrument emitter idiom (pure builder + atomic tmpfs state file). NEW src/pi/splash/boot_battery_test.py (power-tier emitter, placed in splash/ alongside battery_health_emitter.py per that precedent -> same-package reuse of ensureStatesDir/writeStateAtomic, no dup): (1) assessBootBatteryHealth(vcellV) -> (BootBatteryVerdict, reason), PURE + grounded: OK at/above the 3.70V discharge knee; WEAK below it (reason 'vcell-below-healthy-floor', or 'vcell-below-dropout-knee' below the 3.30V buck dropout knee = Drain-7 empirical); UNKNOWN when vcell is None OR outside the 2.5-4.35V physical LiPo band (the classic ~20V un-byte-swapped read -> UNKNOWN, never a confident wrong health = the honest-instrument AC). VERDICT IS VCELL-ONLY: VCELL is a direct register read trustworthy the instant the chip powers up; the SoC% register needs a ~3-min ModelGauge warmup so it is carried as CONTEXT ONLY (socPct + socCalibrated caveat), never the health basis. (2) buildBootBatteryTestState (pure payload: verdict/reason/vcellV/socPct/socCalibrated/ts) -> writes the 'boot-battery-test' state slot. (3) runBootBatteryTest(readVcell, readSoc, statesDir, ...) best-effort: a reader that RAISES resolves to UNKNOWN (a missing/broken fuel gauge must never fail boot) and a state-write failure is logged-never-raised (same contract as the F-103/F-097 emitters). (4) main() CLI (mirrors boot_state_emitter.main) builds real UpsMonitor readers (lazy import so the pure layer stays hardware-free + importable on any host) and always returns 0 -- a boot oneshot unit can invoke it; on a non-Pi/no-gauge host it honestly records UNKNOWN. GROUNDING: dropout knee 3.30V (specs/grounded-knowledge.md Drain-7), discharge knee ~3.70V + healthy AC float ~4.10V (ups_monitor.py), physical band 2.5-4.35V. GATES (in-loop, synchronous): 13 targeted tests GREEN (tests/pi/splash/test_boot_battery_test.py -- assess bands incl. both implausible directions + boundary, payload shape, run writes-file/provisions-dir, reader-raises->UNKNOWN-still-writes, never-raises-on-write-failure, no-soc-reader path); full tests/pi/splash/ GREEN (157 passed / 1 skipped -- no regression from reusing boot_state_emitter primitives). ruff check PASS on both new files. stories.title: idle-poll cold-boot RPM-mask fix (BL-016, Option B; 2nd capture fix; deps US-441)
stories.completionNotes: US-432 CLOSED (bench). idle-poll cold-boot RPM-mask fix (BL-016, Atlas Option B; 2nd capture fix, deps US-441 which is closed). ROOT CAUSE confirmed in code: on a cold-boot-key-OFF connect the US-199 supported-PID probe runs with the engine OFF, so the dark ECU answers 'RPM unsupported' and python-obd caches that in supported_commands for the life of the connection -> every later self.obd.query(RPM) returns a null response WITHOUT sending a 010C frame -> the escalation probe reads None -> drive_start never fires. RPM is in LEGACY_ECU_PARAMETERS (plain path), NOT PARAMETER_DECODERS, so the US-199 LOGGER mask (_assertPidSupported) does NOT gate it -- the only mask suppressing RPM is python-obd's OWN support cache inside obd.query(). So the fix lives at connection.query() (Atlas Option B force read), NOT the logger. CHANGES: (1) obd_connection.py -- new MANDATORY_MODE01_PIDS frozenset({'RPM'}) (grounded: RPM=0x0C is mandatory Mode-01 per SAE J1979, always supported engine-on, so forcing corrects a false-negative not an unsupported PID; deliberately NARROW -- a blanket force re-exposes the 0x42/0x0B/0x15 garbage US-199 skips); new engine-confirmed latch self._forceMandatoryPids (plain atomic bool -- setter never blocks the runLoop behind an in-flight bounded query; query() reads it while already holding _ioLock); setEngineConfirmedForceMandatory(enabled) (idempotent, INFO-logs only on state change so poll-rate RPM reads don't spam) + isForcingMandatoryPids() accessor; query() now calls self.obd.query(command, force=True) via _shouldForceMandatory(command) (resolves command.name or bare-string) ONLY when latch armed AND command in MANDATORY_MODE01_PIDS -- else unchanged self.obd.query(command); disconnect() clears the latch (a fresh connect re-probes -> dark again). (2) core.py -- _maybeEscalateOnAlternatorActiveSignature ARMS the latch (self._setForceMandatoryPids(True)) at the escalation edge (line 1205) BEFORE _injectRpmProbeForEscalation so the probe's OWN read is un-masked; _resetEngineOnEscalation (fired on drive_end, 1264) CLEARS it; new best-effort _setForceMandatoryPids helper (None-connection / missing-seam / exception = WARN no-op, never crashes runLoop). BOTH paths covered by the ONE connection-scoped latch: the escalation probe AND the ongoing realtime poll read through the SAME self._connection wrapper (lifecycle.py:1551 builds the dataLogger with self._connection), so arming the latch un-masks both. (3) simulated_connection.py -- no-op setEngineConfirmedForceMandatory/isForcingMandatoryPids parity (sim obd has no dark-ECU mask). US-388 NON-REGRESSION: read-path only -- evaluateTimeouts / _maybeCloseOnDeadline / _openDriveId / NULL-latch / _startDrive UNTOUCHED; drive_start still fires through the unchanged RPM-sustained machine (detector.py:660-667). GATES (in-loop, synchronous): new tests/pi/obdii/test_obd_connection_force_mandatory.py (12 tests: latch-off-no-force default/regression, latch-on-forces-RPM, latch-does-NOT-force-non-mandatory COOLANT_TEMP = scoped-not-blanket, bare-string RPM forced, latch-clear-returns-to-no-force, disconnect-clears-latch) + 4 new orchestrator wiring tests in test_idle_poll_escalation.py (edge-arms-latch, drive-end-clears-latch, no-connection-clean-no-op, latch-armed-BEFORE-probe-reads ordering) all GREEN; US-441 thread-safety + drive-lifecycle-cold-start + logger_v2_decoders GREEN; full tests/pi/obdii + tests/pi/orchestrator + tests/pi/integration GREEN (exit 0, no regressions). ruff check PASS on all 5 modified files. NOTE FOR PM: mypy (strict) NOT run -- not installed in this dev env (.venv/system python both 'No module named mypy', same as US-441/442/444/445); code fully strict-typed (frozenset[str], bool params/returns, Any command) -- run the mypy gate at integration. LIVE ACCEPTANCE (deferred to CIO car drill, folds into the A-9 re-gate per BENCH-ONLY sprint): after engine-on in the cold-boot-key-OFF sequence, one forced 010C returns real RPM + a drive_start row + non-NULL RPM (the dark-ECU mask no longer suppresses the drive).
